title: 30 documented AI-washing cases and quantitative evidence
scope: 30 purposively selected company/operation cases; not a prevalence estimate. Historical source statuses, not live docket certification.

cases.business_summary: Provided investment advisory services and portfolios.
cases.ai_claim: Claimed AI and machine learning used client data in investment decisions.
cases.why_ai_washing: The SEC found that the advertised capabilities did not exist. This directly fits misrepresented AI use.
cases.stock_market_connection: Private adviser; claims concern investing, not a listed issuer.
cases.limitations: Settled without admitting or denying findings. This does not establish that every part of its service lacked AI.

chart.title: Delphia: civil penalty
chart.headline: US$225,000
chart.interpretation: Civil penalty in the March 2024 settlement.
chart.caveat: Settled without admitting or denying the findings. This amount is not an estimate of investor losses.

cases.business_summary: Offered portfolio analysis and investment advice.
cases.ai_claim: Promoted expert AI-driven forecasts and claimed to be the first regulated AI financial adviser.
cases.why_ai_washing: The SEC found those representations false or misleading, supporting a mismatch between AI positioning and delivered capabilities.
cases.stock_market_connection: Private adviser serving investors.
cases.limitations: Settled without admitting or denying findings; SEC registration is not approval of a product.

chart.title: Global Predictions: civil penalty
chart.headline: US$175,000
chart.interpretation: Civil penalty in the March 2024 settlement.
chart.caveat: The settlement covered the charged conduct, including other violations; it does not measure AI performance.

cases.business_summary: Raised funds for an advisory business and managed client accounts.
cases.ai_claim: Claimed an AI platform performed automated securities trading.
cases.why_ai_washing: The SEC found the business was falsely described as having this platform. AI claims helped solicit investors and advisory clients.
cases.stock_market_connection: Private fundraising plus trading in client securities accounts.
cases.limitations: Entities and individuals settled without admitting or denying findings; other misconduct was also involved.

chart.title: Rimar: penalties by individual
chart.headline: US$310,000 combined
chart.interpretation: Sum of the two civil penalties.
chart.caveat: Penalties are separate from disgorgement and interest. They are not the amount raised or investor losses.

cases.business_summary: Supplied voice-assisted drive-through ordering systems.
cases.ai_claim: Claimed its AI removed human order-taking and reported misleading non-intervention rates.
cases.why_ai_washing: The SEC found extensive human intervention and misleading disclosure of third-party technology. Automation claims overstated the product's independence.
cases.stock_market_connection: Nasdaq-listed until September 2024; disclosure concerned public investors.
cases.limitations: Settled without admitting or denying findings. Third-party technology and human support are legitimate when accurately disclosed.

chart.title: Presto: orders requiring human help
chart.headline: Human help remained substantial
chart.interpretation: Share of orders requiring intervention described in the SEC order.
chart.caveat: These are different versions and periods, not a controlled before-and-after experiment or a claimed-versus-tested accuracy comparison.

cases.business_summary: Operated advertising technology and promoted an AI fraud-detection tool.
cases.ai_claim: Touted successful KAI tests and associated revenue in stock-offering materials.
cases.why_ai_washing: Fabricated test reports and revenue misrepresented product efficacy and commercial validation. This combines AI capability inflation with accounting fraud.
cases.stock_market_connection: IPO and secondary public offering in 2020.
cases.limitations: The former CEO pleaded guilty; this does not establish culpability of every employee or prove that KAI never existed.

chart.title: Kubient: fabricated revenue
chart.headline: US$1.3 million
chart.interpretation: Fabricated revenue described in the DOJ sentencing announcement.
chart.caveat: Revenue fabrication is not the same as cash raised, AI accuracy, or shareholder losses.

cases.business_summary: Managed trades in clients' brokerage accounts under the WOLO Wealth name.
cases.ai_claim: Claimed proprietary AI fully automated trading and eliminated downside risk.
cases.why_ai_washing: The SEC alleges the purported software was not used for the described trades. If substantiated, this is misrepresented AI deployment coupled with impossible risk assurances.
cases.stock_market_connection: Client brokerage accounts and options trading; not a listed company.
cases.limitations: Complaint allegations, not a liability finding. WOLO was a business name, not an incorporated entity, according to the complaint.

chart.title: WOLO Wealth: alleged client losses
chart.headline: > US$1.6 million
chart.interpretation: Losses alleged by the SEC by January 2023.
chart.caveat: The lower-bound bar covers the broader alleged advisory fraud, not losses causally isolated to AI. These remain complaint allegations.

cases.business_summary: Offered a chatbot and tools for consumer legal tasks.
cases.ai_claim: Promoted a robot lawyer able to substitute for professional legal expertise.
cases.why_ai_washing: The FTC challenged claims unsupported by adequate evaluation. The pattern is overstated professional capability, even where AI is genuinely used.
cases.stock_market_connection: Consumer service; no public-stock claim assessed.
cases.limitations: A settlement is not a trial finding that every feature failed.

chart.title: DoNotPay: settlement payment
chart.headline: US$193,000
chart.interpretation: Payment under the FTC settlement.
chart.caveat: This is a settlement amount, not a measured legal-task error rate or the total harm to customers.

cases.business_summary: Offered a shopping app for completing purchases across retail websites.
cases.ai_claim: Presented checkout as autonomously completed by proprietary AI.
cases.why_ai_washing: DOJ alleges human contractors secretly completed purchases while the automation rate was effectively zero. If proven, this fits concealed manual work and fictitious autonomy.
cases.stock_market_connection: Private startup fundraising.
cases.limitations: The cited indictment announcement is not a conviction or a check of the current docket.

chart.title: Nate: capital raised
chart.headline: > US$40 million
chart.interpretation: Fundraising described in the DOJ indictment announcement.
chart.caveat: The source alleges near-zero automation but supplies no precise tested percentage. Funding is not a finding that every dollar was lost.

cases.business_summary: Sold facial-recognition software for security systems.
cases.ai_claim: Claimed high accuracy, no gender or racial bias, and spoof resistance.
cases.why_ai_washing: The FTC alleged insufficient support for broad efficacy and fairness claims. This fits unsupported AI performance assurances.
cases.stock_market_connection: Security software; no public-stock claim assessed.
cases.limitations: AI existence is not disputed here. The concern is how performance was represented.

chart.title: IntelliVision: training-data scale
chart.headline: ≈100,000 unique individuals
chart.interpretation: FTC allegation about the underlying training images.
chart.caveat: The company claimed millions of faces. Augmented variants of the same faces are not additional unique people; no exact advertised count is invented.

cases.business_summary: Sold an automated website accessibility tool.
cases.ai_claim: Claimed the tool could make any website WCAG-compliant.
cases.why_ai_washing: The FTC alleged misleading or unsupported compliance claims. The pattern is promoting an AI tool as sufficient for a broader outcome than demonstrated.
cases.assessment: Strong documented concern: FTC final order
cases.stock_market_connection: Business software; no public-stock claim assessed.
cases.limitations: This does not imply that all automated accessibility assistance lacks value.

chart.title: accessiBe: consumer relief
chart.headline: US$1 million
chart.interpretation: Payment required under the FTC settlement.
chart.caveat: This is not an accessibility failure rate or a count of inaccessible websites.

cases.business_summary: Sold a tool for identifying AI-generated text.
cases.ai_claim: Advertised 98% detection accuracy across content.
cases.why_ai_washing: The FTC reported approximately 53% accuracy on general-purpose content. Extrapolating narrower performance to broader uses fits inflated AI accuracy.
cases.assessment: Strong documented concern: FTC final order
cases.stock_market_connection: Content software; no public-stock claim assessed.
cases.limitations: The test result applies to the evaluated content and version, not all detectors or future versions.

chart.title: Workado: advertised vs. tested accuracy
chart.headline: 45 percentage points
chart.interpretation: Advertised accuracy minus the test result reported by the FTC.
chart.caveat: The test concerns general-purpose content. The FTC alleged training or fine-tuning on academic content; the result is not a universal score for all uses.

cases.business_summary: Sold screening systems to schools and other venues.
cases.ai_claim: Promoted AI screening as detecting weapons while ignoring harmless items, with superior performance.
cases.why_ai_washing: The FTC challenged efficacy claims. This fits overstated AI capability in a safety-sensitive product marketed by a public company.
cases.stock_market_connection: Public-company product claims; not evidence of a particular stock-price effect.
cases.limitations: The issue is performance claims, not proof that the system used no AI. Settlement terms do not establish every allegation.

chart.title: Evolv: false alarms after a setting change

points.label: False alarm rate at the cited school

chart.headline: 1 in 2 screenings flagged
chart.interpretation: FTC account of a school increasing sensitivity after a missed knife.
chart.caveat: One school and setting, not a product-wide benchmark. A false-alarm rate is not the percentage of weapons missed.

cases.business_summary: Operated an anonymous messaging app.
cases.ai_claim: Claimed AI moderation would protect users from cyberbullying.
cases.why_ai_washing: The FTC alleged that promised AI safeguards did not filter harmful messages as represented. This fits overstated AI safety assurances.
cases.stock_market_connection: Consumer app; no public-stock claim assessed.
cases.limitations: Other allegations concerned billing and children’s privacy; inclusion here is specifically about moderation claims.

chart.title: NGL: settlement components
chart.headline: US$5 million combined
chart.interpretation: Consumer relief plus a separate civil penalty.
chart.caveat: The case also covered child privacy, billing, and other conduct. The total cannot be attributed solely to AI moderation claims.

cases.business_summary: Marketed conversational AI services and business opportunities to entrepreneurs.
cases.ai_claim: Promised business growth, substantial earnings, and refund protection.
cases.why_ai_washing: The FTC challenged performance, profitability, and refund representations. AI branding supported outcomes that allegedly were not substantiated.
cases.assessment: Conditional: FTC allegations and proposed order
cases.stock_market_connection: Small-business purchases; not a stock offering.
cases.limitations: This concerns misleading claims around AI, not a finding that AI was absent. The cited release describes a proposed court order.

chart.title: Air AI: judgment vs. payable relief
chart.headline: Most of the judgment suspended
chart.interpretation: The proposed terms distinguish face value from the amount payable.
chart.caveat: A largely suspended judgment is not US$18 million recovered. The very short second bar uses the same scale; the announcement described a proposed order.

cases.business_summary: Sold services to establish and operate online storefronts.
cases.ai_claim: Advertised AI tools for rapidly generating passive income.
cases.why_ai_washing: The FTC alleged that promised earnings generally failed to materialize. The AI-washing pattern is an unsupported business outcome attributed to AI.
cases.assessment: Conditional: FTC allegations and proposed order
cases.stock_market_connection: Consumer business opportunities, not publicly traded securities.
cases.limitations: Poor returns alone are not AI washing; inclusion rests on the alleged deceptive AI-linked earnings pitch. The cited announcement describes a proposed order.

chart.title: Ascend: proposed monetary judgment
chart.headline: US$25 million face value
chart.interpretation: Monetary judgment in the proposed settlement.
chart.caveat: Partially suspended based on inability to pay. Do not interpret face value as the cash distributed to consumers.

cases.business_summary: Sold managed online-store business opportunities.
cases.ai_claim: Promised guaranteed income from storefronts using AI software.
cases.why_ai_washing: The FTC challenged deceptive earnings guarantees tied to purported AI-powered stores. This fits unsupported AI-enabled profitability.
cases.assessment: Conditional: FTC allegations and proposed order
cases.stock_market_connection: Consumer business opportunities, not a stock-market investment product.
cases.limitations: Treat both names as one case. The record does not by itself prove all underlying software lacked AI. The cited announcement describes a proposed order.

chart.title: FBA Machine: proposed monetary judgment
chart.headline: US$15.7 million face value
chart.interpretation: Monetary judgment described in the FTC announcement.
chart.caveat: Partially suspended based on inability to pay; the bar does not show recovered funds.

cases.business_summary: Sold training and done-for-you online stores.
cases.ai_claim: Marketed an AI-powered e-commerce business capable of substantial profits.
cases.why_ai_washing: The FTC alleged that the promoted profits did not materialize. AI was used to support an allegedly deceptive opportunity pitch.
cases.assessment: Strong documented concern: FTC settlement announcement
cases.stock_market_connection: Consumer business opportunities.
cases.limitations: Distinct from Automators’ former Empire Ecommerce brand. This is an earnings-claim case, not a finding that AI was absent.

chart.title: Ecommerce Empire Builders: judgment
chart.headline: US$9.79 million, rounded
chart.interpretation: Court-entered judgment described by the FTC.
chart.caveat: Partially suspended; asset transfers fund relief. The judgment is not a measured recovery total.

cases.business_summary: Set up third-party online stores and sold business coaching.
cases.ai_claim: Claimed AI could help ensure store profitability and high passive earnings.
cases.why_ai_washing: The FTC challenged unfounded income and profit claims connected to AI. This fits overstated AI business benefits.
cases.stock_market_connection: Consumer business opportunities.
cases.limitations: Automators, Empire Ecommerce, and Onyx Distribution are grouped as one operation; not three cases.

chart.title: Automators: money invested
chart.headline: US$22 million
chart.interpretation: Consumer investment amount reported in the FTC case summary.
chart.caveat: Amount invested is not necessarily the amount lost or recovered. Related Automators, Empire and Onyx entities count as one operation.

cases.business_summary: Sold managed storefronts to people seeking passive income.
cases.ai_claim: Promised high passive earnings through a proprietary AI-powered system.
cases.why_ai_washing: The FTC complaint expressly alleges false AI and affiliation claims. This supports both misrepresented technology and unsupported profit promises.
cases.assessment: Conditional: FTC complaint and settlement announcement
cases.stock_market_connection: Consumer business opportunities.
cases.limitations: The case page describes an August proposed settlement. Do not equate that wording with adjudicated liability.

chart.title: Click Profit: Amazon store restrictions
chart.headline: ≈95% of its Amazon stores
chart.interpretation: Store restrictions alleged in the FTC complaint.
chart.caveat: This concerns Click Profit's Amazon stores, not all Amazon sellers. It is not a model-accuracy measure or a proven AI-caused suspension rate.

cases.business_summary: Sold app-development services supported by software tools and human teams.
cases.ai_claim: Marketed AI-assisted app creation as fast and simple.
cases.why_ai_washing: Reporting based on former-employee interviews describes more manual delivery than the marketing suggested. This is a plausible overstatement-of-automation pattern.
cases.stock_market_connection: Venture-backed private startup; not Microsoft’s own operating business.
cases.limitations: Former CEO Manpreet Ratia denied misleading users and said the platform automated meaningful work. Earlier representatives described human-assisted AI. Reporting does not establish that no AI existed; insolvency is not proof.

chart.title: Builder.ai: advertised automation

points.label: App or website claimed buildable autonomously

chart.headline: Actual comparable rate: not disclosed
chart.interpretation: Founder claim reported by Rest of World; no measured comparison is available.
chart.caveat: Former staff described much more manual work. Management denied fake-AI characterizations. The bar shows a disputed claim, not validated performance.

cases.business_summary: Developed a proposed humanoid home assistant.
cases.ai_claim: Marketed an advanced AI robot for delivery in 2023.
cases.why_ai_washing: The SEC alleged the robot was much less developed than represented, with no realistic prospect of the promised delivery.
cases.stock_market_connection: Private startup fundraising; not a listed security.
cases.limitations: The CEO consented without admitting or denying the allegations; the release described a settlement subject to court approval.

chart.title: Destiny Robotics: fundraising scale
chart.headline: ≈US$141,000 raised
chart.interpretation: Fundraising described in the SEC complaint announcement.
chart.caveat: Fundraising is context, not a valuation, investor-loss estimate, or robot-performance metric.

cases.business_summary: Sold memberships linked to future software subscriptions and referral commissions.
cases.ai_claim: Promoted passive income from an ecosystem of AI applications.
cases.why_ai_washing: The SEC alleged that no applications had commercially launched and no commissions had been paid by June 2023 despite years of soliciting investors.
cases.assessment: Alleged availability and AI-linked earnings mismatch
cases.stock_market_connection: Investment-contract allegations; not an exchange-listed AI stock.
cases.limitations: The cited complaint is an allegation. A delayed launch does not by itself establish that AI was technically absent.

chart.title: ONPASSIVE: investment raised
chart.headline: > US$108 million
chart.interpretation: Amount alleged in the SEC's August 2023 announcement.
chart.caveat: The cited historical cutoff is June 2023. Fundraising does not establish how much was lost or that later products never launched.

cases.business_summary: Solicited investments in purported algorithmic asset management.
cases.ai_claim: Promised extraordinary returns and full capital protection through proprietary AI.
cases.why_ai_washing: The SEC alleged false AI-related investment promises, misleading regulatory assurances and misappropriation of investor money.
cases.stock_market_connection: The SEC also alleged false statements about a Nasdaq listing application; this does not establish an actual listing.
cases.limitations: Allegations in a complaint, not a trial finding. The loss figure covers the broader alleged scheme.

chart.title: QZ Asset: alleged investor harm
chart.headline: At least US$6 million
chart.interpretation: Amount described in the SEC complaint announcement.
chart.caveat: This is a lower bound for the alleged scheme, not a stock-market loss estimate or an AI error rate.

cases.business_summary: Offered investments in a purported automated crypto trading bot.
cases.ai_claim: Claimed AI could generate daily returns of up to 2.2%.
cases.why_ai_washing: Montana alleged unsubstantiated AI trading profits and reliance on new deposits; an audit also contradicted advertised withdrawal terms.
cases.assessment: Alleged unsupported AI earnings and misleading terms
cases.stock_market_connection: Crypto investment solicitation, not a listed company.
cases.limitations: The source is a temporary cease-and-desist order and proposed agency action. The lockup comparison measures contract terms, not model performance.

chart.title: YieldTrust: advertised vs. audited lockup
chart.headline: 2× the advertised lockup
chart.interpretation: Audit finding summarized in Montana's order, paragraphs 14–15.
chart.caveat: A terms mismatch in an AI-branded offering; it does not measure AI profitability. The cited order is a temporary agency action.

cases.business_summary: Collected bitcoin for a purported forex trading pool.
cases.ai_claim: Promoted a proprietary automated trading bot; the CFTC identifies the scheme in its AI-bot advisory.
cases.why_ai_washing: A court found the bot representation false and bitcoin misappropriated. The AI narrative concealed a fraudulent investment operation.
cases.assessment: Strong: court findings and CFTC AI advisory
cases.stock_market_connection: Unregistered commodity pool; not an exchange-listed issuer.
cases.limitations: The cited default judgment is against Steynberg. Ordered restitution and penalties do not establish that money was recovered.

sources.title: CFTC advisory on AI trading bots

chart.title: Mirror Trading: ordered payments
chart.headline: US$3.47 billion combined, rounded
chart.interpretation: Two distinct components of the default judgment.
chart.caveat: Neither amount establishes actual recovery. The bitcoin valuation underlying restitution is historical, not today's bitcoin price.

cases.business_summary: Sells iPhones and associated AI software features.
cases.ai_claim: Advertised Apple Intelligence features as available at the iPhone 16 launch.
cases.why_ai_washing: NAD found that availability disclosures did not adequately qualify features delivered later. This fits overstated present availability, not nonexistent AI.
cases.stock_market_connection: Public issuer: product messaging can shape expectations about device upgrades; no stock-price effect is quantified here.
cases.limitations: NAD is industry self-regulation, not a government agency. Apple disagreed with findings about features available by the decision but agreed to follow recommendations. The withdrawn Siri video was not adjudicated on its merits.

sources.title: BBB National Programs / NAD decision announcement

chart.title: Apple: availability claims reviewed
chart.headline: Availability, not AI accuracy
chart.interpretation: Counts of explicitly named examples in the NAD release.
chart.caveat: Five: Priority Notifications, Image Playground, Genmoji, Image Wand, ChatGPT integration. Three: onscreen awareness, personal context, cross-app actions. This is not a failure rate or a claim about 2026 availability.

cases.business_summary: Sold bookkeeping and back-office services to small businesses.
cases.ai_claim: Presented AI automation as a replacement for substantial accounting work.
cases.why_ai_washing: Forbes reported that employees and outsourced accountants did much of the work the product was marketed as automating.
cases.assessment: Reported autonomy mismatch; no adjudication cited
cases.stock_market_connection: Venture-backed startup; the funding figure is private capital, not public-market capitalization.
cases.limitations: Human assistance alone is not AI washing. The issue is the reported gap with automation claims. The founder blamed pandemic-related demand loss and described the ambition to automate small-business back offices.

chart.title: ScaleFactor: venture funding
chart.headline: US$100 million
chart.interpretation: Funding reported by Forbes in July 2020.
chart.caveat: Funding measures scale, not proven losses. No independent automation percentage is supplied, so none is plotted.

cases.business_summary: Solicited investors through social messaging and a purported trading platform.
cases.ai_claim: Claimed to provide AI trading signals.
cases.why_ai_washing: The SEC alleged that displayed trading profits were fabricated and trades never occurred.
cases.assessment: Strong alleged fictitious AI trading service
cases.stock_market_connection: Retail investment solicitation; not a listed stock.
cases.limitations: Complaint allegations. The amount concerns alleged misappropriation, not an AI accuracy result.

chart.title: Cryptoaiml: alleged misappropriation
chart.headline: > US$12.5 million
chart.interpretation: Amount alleged by the SEC.
chart.caveat: Lower-bound bar; allegations are not adjudicated losses.

cases.business_summary: Offered rental of purported trading bots.
cases.ai_claim: Promised guaranteed returns from AI bots.
cases.why_ai_washing: The SEC alleged that the bots did not exist and investor funds were not used to generate trading returns.
cases.stock_market_connection: Retail crypto investment scheme; separate complaint from Cryptoaiml.
cases.limitations: Complaint allegations, not adjudicated findings. Related TSAI entities are grouped as one operation.

chart.title: TSAI Pro: alleged misappropriation
chart.headline: > US$2.8 million
chart.interpretation: Amount alleged by the SEC.
chart.caveat: Lower-bound bar; separate from the Cryptoaiml complaint.

cases.business_summary: Solicited loans to fund a leveraged forex trading pool.
cases.ai_claim: Claimed an AI bot would recover losses and repay participants.
cases.why_ai_washing: The CFTC alleged false AI recovery assurances after millions in losses, alongside misappropriation and payments using new investors' money.
cases.assessment: Strong alleged unsupported AI recovery promise
cases.stock_market_connection: Commodity pool investment, not a listed AI stock.
cases.limitations: The cited complaint contains allegations. Losses preceded the AI recovery claim; the chart does not measure an AI model's trading performance.

sources.title: CFTC Technical Trading Team complaint announcement

chart.title: Technical Trading Team: funds and losses
chart.headline: > US$3.13 million trading losses
chart.interpretation: CFTC allegations about losses preceding the AI recovery pitch.
chart.caveat: The bars describe related funds, not additive totals. They do not show losses from a deployed AI system.
